Name of the Surah

• It is called "al-Qamar" (The Moon) because it opens with the event of the splitting of the moon, which is one of the miracles by which Allah supported our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Warning of the approach of the Resurrection and of the hardships people will face at the time of resurrection, when they come out of the graves as if they were scattered locusts.

• Calling the polytheists to take heed and reflect upon the scenes of punishment and torment that befell the tyrants and arrogant ones in this world, because they denied Allah's messengers, and that they will face what those (earlier peoples) faced; and warning them of what is even more severe than that, namely the Day of Resurrection and the terrors it contains.

[The Tafsir]

The Hour has drawn near, and the moon was split in two, when the disbelievers of Makkah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to show them a sign. He called upon Allah, and He showed them that sign.

If the disbelievers see a sign and proof of the truthfulness of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), they turn away from faith in him and from affirming him, denying and rejecting, and they say after the sign has become evident: "This is passing magic, false, vanishing, with no lasting existence."

They denied the Prophet (ﷺ) and followed their misguidance and what their desires invited them to, of denial. And every matter, whether good or evil, will befall its people on the Day of Resurrection, when reward and punishment become manifest.

So turn away from them, Messenger, and await for them a momentous day: the day when the angel calls, by blowing into the trumpet (al-Qarn), to a dreadful and terrible matter, namely the standing for reckoning.
